incumbent.name: Elizabeth Rowray
incumbent.summary: Elizabeth Rowray, a Yorktown nonprofit consultant and former Yorktown school board member, has represented House District 35 since 2020 {caucus_rowray}. She serves on the Ways and Means; Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; and Family, Children and Human Affairs committees {caucus_rowray} {caucus_committees_2024}.
record: Committees: Ways and Means; Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; Family, Children and Human Affairs {caucus_rowray}. 2025 interim appointments: Indiana Protection and Advocacy Services Commission, Doula Reimbursement Advisory Board and the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Holiday Commission {caucus_interim_2025}.

2023 session: Authored HB 1568 to let pharmacists prescribe hormonal contraceptives to women 18 and older after a self-screening; the House Public Health Committee approved it in February 2023 {caucus_hb1568}.

2025 session: Authored HEA 1248, which expands Child Care and Development Fund eligibility for foster families and reserves 200 vouchers for children with licensed foster parents {caucus_hea1248}. Sponsored SEA 491, letting Alexandria annex noncontiguous land for an industrial park {caucus_sea491}, and SB 498 on qualifications for DCS casework supervisors {caucus_sb498}.

April 10, 2025: Voted yes when the House passed SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, 65-29 {rc_sea1_433}. April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the 2025 state budget conference report (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}.
Dec. 5, 2025: Voted yes on HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}.

2026 session: Authored HEA 1357, requiring staff at child caring institutions, group homes and child placing agencies to undergo federal background checks every four years; ceremonially signed in May 2026 {caucus_hea1357}.

race_context: House District 35 includes parts of Delaware and Madison counties {caucus_rowray}; the Herald Bulletin describes it as including most of northern Madison County {hb_rematch}.
The race is a rematch of 2024, when Rowray defeated Gift with 71% of the vote {hb_rematch} {wiki_2026}.
Rowray and Gift were the only candidates listed in their parties' May 5, 2026 primaries {wiki_2026}; both are on the November ballot {in_list}.

Key differences: Gift opposes expanding private school vouchers, wants an end to partisan gerrymandering and supports legalizing adult-use marijuana {gift_issues} {gift_home}; Rowray voted for the 2025 budget and the 2025 redistricting bill {rc_hb1001_576} {rc_hb1032_28}. Gift says he opposes data center development {gift_home}; no statement from Rowray on data centers was found.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Elizabeth Rowray is the Republican incumbent, first elected in 2020 {caucus_rowray}. Her recent bills have focused on child welfare, foster care and child care {caucus_hea1248} {caucus_hea1357}.
background: Nonprofit consultant; lives in Yorktown; graduated from Muncie Burris High School and Ball State University {caucus_rowray}.
Former legislative director for U.S. Rep. Mark Souder; worked at the Muncie-Delaware County Economic Development Alliance; served on the Yorktown school board {caucus_rowray}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for a fourth term in January 2026 {hb_rematch}; listed as the only Republican candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Said of HEA 1248: "Child care costs should never stand in the way of families who are willing to foster" {caucus_hea1248_sign}.
Said of HEA 1357: "Families deserve confidence that children placed in state-regulated care are surrounded by qualified and trustworthy adults" {caucus_hea1357}.
Said pharmacist-prescribed contraceptives "will greatly expand access to thousands of Hoosier women" (2023) {caucus_hb1568}.
Said SEA 491 "could be a game changer" for Alexandria's economic development {caucus_sea491}; the caucus says she scored above 90% on the Indiana Chamber's 2025 scorecard {caucus_chamber}.
Voted for SEA 1 (2025) {rc_sea1_433}; the caucus listed it among the bills on the Chamber scorecard {caucus_chamber}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Rowray about Gift were found.
plans: After the 2026 session, said her focus was "delivering results for our district" through tax relief and more efficient government {caucus_session_2026}.
endorsements_finance: The House Republican caucus says Rowray scored above 90% on the Indiana Chamber of Commerce's 2025 legislator scorecard {caucus_chamber}.
gaps: No 2026 campaign website, survey responses or campaign statements were found; WFYI's voter guide for District 35 could not be located.
Final outcome of HB 1568 (2023) and SB 498 (2025) not confirmed.

candidates.summary: Phil Gift is a retired Veterans Affairs nurse from Gaston, running as a Democrat for the second straight cycle {sp_gift} {gift_about}. He focuses on public school funding, rural health care, opposition to data centers and legalizing marijuana {gift_home}.
background: Registered nurse who spent 17 years with the Department of Veterans Affairs, including as a triage nurse at the Marion VA Medical Center and patient care manager at the Muncie VA clinic {gift_about}.
Raised in Fairmount; degrees from Vincennes University, the University of Cincinnati and Ball State University {gift_about}. Lives in Gaston {sp_gift}.
Was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024 {sp_gift} {indems_2024}.
path_to_ballot: Filed in January 2026 {hb_rematch}; listed as the only Democratic candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Says Indiana "should fully fund its public schools and stop expanding taxpayer-funded private school vouchers" {gift_issues}.
Wants to protect farmland and water from "unchecked data center development" that he says offers few long-term jobs while receiving large tax incentives {gift_home}.
Says residential customers "shouldn't subsidize massive new energy demands"; supports more transparency in utility rate cases and stronger IURC oversight {gift_issues}.
Wants to keep rural hospitals open and expand access to affordable insurance {gift_home}.
Supports workforce-housing construction, fewer building barriers and rehabilitation of aging homes {gift_issues}.
Supports legalizing, regulating and taxing adult-use marijuana with expungement review for low-level possession {gift_issues}.

on_incumbent: No direct statements about Rowray or her record were found; Gift says he is "determined to bring fresh leadership and real change to our community" {sp_gift}.
plans: Top priorities: "securing strong, well-funded public education for every child, access to affordable health care and housing, and providing a living wage for all Hoosiers" {sp_gift}.
endorsements_finance: In 2024 the Indiana Democratic Party chair praised Gift's VA experience when promoting his candidacy {indems_2024}. No 2026 endorsements or fundraising found.
gaps: Little news coverage of the 2026 race; WFYI's District 35 guide was not found.
The Herald Bulletin article also says Gift ran against Rowray in 2022; other sources reviewed mention only 2024. Unresolved.
Middle initial "G." from the ballot list only; age not verified.
